notes: Bunker is the most door-dense stage in the game by a wide margin, and the fewest spawns of any converted map. Those two numbers define it: movement is almost entirely through thresholds, and reappearances are predictable enough to punish.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: This stage is built almost entirely from doorways, so there is barely any open space and nearly every contact happens at a threshold.
nuance.because: The arena carries thirty-six Door records, more than any other multiplayer stage.

nuance.claim: With movement funnelled through doors everywhere, mines make large parts of the map genuinely impassable and this becomes the most oppressive mine stage in the game.
nuance.because: Thirty-six Door records against only one hundred and twenty-one pads is the densest door-to-space ratio of any stage.

nuance.claim: This is the only converted map with as few spawn points as the tightest dedicated arenas, so spawn denial is a real strategy here rather than opportunism.
nuance.because: The arena carries five Spawn records, against seven or eight on the other converted maps.

nuance.claim: The stage is physically small, so contacts are constant and there is little opportunity to reload or reposition unmolested.
nuance.because: One hundred and twenty-one pads is the smallest of any converted arena.

nuance.claim: There is nowhere on the map with a long clear line, so precision weapons have no role and rate of fire decides fights.
The rooms are too small to fire explosives without catching yourself, so those sets play badly here.
Because everything is doors, every move is announced by one opening; surprise comes from timing rather than from stealth.
Banks of monitors and screens break up the interior further, giving small pockets of cover in rooms that otherwise have none.
nuance.because: The arena carries eight SingleMonitor and two HangingMonitor records.

nuance.claim: The most defensible positions are the rooms with one door, because the door-heavy layout means most rooms have several.
One-hit kills in a map of doorways means whoever opens a door first usually dies, so the mode rewards waiting for someone else to move.
An unarmed carrier has almost nowhere to run in a small door-locked map, so holds are short and the mode becomes a rapid exchange of the flag.
Pickups are the normalised conversion set, so neither armour nor ammunition is scarce enough to fight over; position is the only real resource.
nuance.because: The arena carries the standard conversion loadout of two Armour, sixteen AmmoBox and nine Collectable records.

nuance.claim: The stage is dimly lit throughout, so darker characters gain a small but real advantage at the ranges the map actually fights at.
